```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# readr rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "" rather than NA
analysts <- readr::read_csv("../../data/analysts5.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
curve <- readr::read_csv("../../data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
original <- readr::read_csv("../../data/housing_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
housing <- readr::read_csv("../../data/housing_emails.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

fmt <- \(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d) |> sub(pattern = "^-", replacement = "−")
an <- \(id, col) analysts[[col]][analysts$id == id]

# The Task 3 target, on the public file of the OAs: Hispanic against all other
# names among the coded replies, with and without the continuity correction
chi_tab <- original |>
  datawizard::data_filter(Response_Dichotomous == 1 & !is.na(ProperName)) |>
  stats::xtabs(formula = ~ startsWith(TreatmentGroup, "Hispanic") + ProperName, data = _)
chi_yates <- unname(stats::chisq.test(chi_tab)$statistic)
chi_plain <- unname(stats::chisq.test(chi_tab, correct = FALSE)$statistic)

# The same for 25N5D: the delivered emails to Hispanic and white names, a
# missing reply counted as no greeting, with and without the correction that
# prop.test() applies by default
counts_25n5d <- original |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(Response_Dichotomous) & !grepl("^black", TreatmentGroup)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup),
                          greeted = Response_Dichotomous == 1 & ProperName %in% 1) |>
  datawizard::data_summary(greetings = sum(greeted), emails = n(), by = "hispanic_name")
prop_yates <- unname(stats::prop.test(counts_25n5d$greetings, counts_25n5d$emails)$statistic)
prop_plain <- unname(stats::prop.test(counts_25n5d$greetings, counts_25n5d$emails, correct = FALSE)$statistic)
stopifnot(abs(prop_yates - an("25N5D", "statistic_recorded")) < 0.0015)
```

## The claim

Five independent analysts reanalysed one claim of the original authors (OAs) [@EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect] in the robustness study. The claim, as the analysts received it, was:

> "Hispanic housing applicants were ... less likely to be greeted by name than were ... white counterparts" (p. 100 of the published article)

The published result behind it is the coefficient of the Hispanic names in a logistic regression of a named greeting on the three groups of names, with community controls and the Hard Email indicator: **−0.82 (standard error 0.22) on 549 replies**, which the OAs translate into a gap of **−20.0 percentage points** in the probability of a named greeting, with a 95% confidence interval from −30.5 to −10.0. The data come from an experiment: `r format(nrow(housing), big.mark = ",")` emails to housing authorities, each of which was signed with one of six names that were assigned at random.

## The five analysts {#the-five-analysts}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-five
#| tbl-cap: "The five reanalyses, with the statistic recorded in the robustness study and the gap in percentage points by the workshop's refit. Source: `data/analysts5.csv`."
#| echo: false
analysts |>
  datawizard::data_modify(
    Comparison = sub(" vs ", " against ", comparison),
    `Recorded statistic` = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(statistic_recorded) ~ "none recorded",
      statistic_type == "chi2" ~ paste0("χ<sup>2</sup> = ", fmt(statistic_recorded, 3)),
      .default = paste(statistic_type, "=", fmt(statistic_recorded, 3))
    ),
    `Gap (points)` = fmt(b_pp_refit)
  ) |>
  datawizard::data_select(c(Analyst = "id", "Comparison", `Emails counted` = "population",
                            "Recorded statistic", "Gap (points)",
                            `Conclusion in Task 1` = "task1")) |>
  tinytable::tt() |>
  tinytable::style_tt(j = 5, align = "r")
```

All five found Hispanic names greeted by name less often than the comparison names, and all four recorded statistics reproduce exactly on the public file. Two of the five nevertheless concluded in Task 1 of the robustness study that the data showed no evidence either way, and the [background page](../../background.qmd#sec-reanalysts) sets out what question each analyst answered.
